svg.aria-label: How do data, learning, and machine limits shape a deployable ML system?

a.xlink:title: Examples used to fit model parameters; their coverage and labels help determine learned behavior.
The predictions a trained model produces on inputs, whose usefulness and physical deliverability must both be established.
Time spent moving data, performing arithmetic, and paying system overhead; the applicable overlap model depends on the execution boundary.
The amount of resident model and runtime state a machine can hold; fitting is a feasibility condition before speed is considered.
The allowed rate of energy consumption, limited by battery supply and heat dissipation.
Placing computation near the data when transfer delay or bandwidth makes remote execution infeasible.
Operationally measurable targets and constraints that determine what counts as a successful system.
A checked specification of the inputs, outputs, and invariants at a pipeline boundary.
A decision that blocks deployment unless a particular artifact meets declared evaluation thresholds.
Supervision targets that specify the behavior the model is trained to reproduce.
Information crossing training, validation, or test boundaries so evaluation ceases to estimate generalization.
The storage, decoding, transformation, and transfer stages that deliver usable examples to the accelerator.
Agreement between the feature values produced by training and serving transformations for the same raw request.
A shared arithmetic primitive for dense layers and lowered neural-network operations.
Forward intermediate tensors retained because backward derivative rules need their values.
Derivatives of training loss with respect to parameters, used to update those parameters.
Resident weights, saved activations, gradients, and optimizer state required during training.
A structural assumption encoded by an architecture that restricts its hypothesis space and changes learning and execution costs.
An operation that lets tokens combine information from other positions; dense score computation grows quadratically with sequence length.
A reverse traversal that computes parameter gradients from a scalar loss using recorded forward operations.
Host-side work paid to submit operations; many short kernels can make it dominate device execution.
Combining operations to reduce dispatches and keep intermediate values in local storage when dependencies and resource limits permit.
Elapsed training time needed to reach a stated quality threshold, coupling convergence work with achieved execution rate.
Achieved model arithmetic divided by the relevant peak arithmetic rate; useful work differs from device busy time.
Retaining selected forward tensors and recomputing discarded intermediates during backward to reduce activation memory.
The time or resource cost of scoring and filtering examples before or during training.
Selected examples retained for training, whose value must be checked against quality and coverage constraints.
Allocation of a fixed training compute budget between parameter count and training data within a fitted scaling regime.
Representing tensors at lower precision to reduce storage and traffic, subject to quality and runtime support.
Zero-valued or removed weights whose storage and execution benefit depends on pattern, metadata, and sparse kernels.
Partitioning operations so operand blocks can be reused in local memory rather than repeatedly fetched from off-chip memory.
Using a locally retained operand for multiple arithmetic operations before fetching it again.
The fraction of baseline end-to-end time that an optimization can accelerate; the remaining time limits total gain.
The workload, software, hardware, measurement boundary, and run rules required to interpret and reproduce a result.
Task-relevant predictive performance evaluated over appropriate distributions and subgroups, with uncertainty.
A target for the fraction of requests completing within a stated latency boundary.
A change in serving inputs or outcomes relative to the evaluated distribution; input divergence alone does not establish quality loss.
Observation of infrastructure, input statistics, and model outcomes used to detect and diagnose production changes.
Recovery to a known-good artifact and configuration when a release violates operational bounds.
Declared error or decision-rate criteria measured across specified population slices and enforced at release.
A feedback mechanism in which model decisions alter future observations and training data, potentially amplifying disparity.
Emissions attributable to electricity use under a stated accounting boundary and electricity carbon intensity.
Supplying operands takes time. For a fixed memory level, the transfer lower bound is bytes moved divided by bandwidth.
The arithmetic lower bound is the required operations divided by the available compute rate. Faster operand delivery cannot remove this bound.
Bandwidth limits the rate at which an accelerator receives operands from a given memory level. The relevant level depends on data placement and reuse.
Operations per byte moved identifies the compute-versus-bandwidth regime. A suitable batch can reuse weights and raise this ratio.
Lower precision reduces the bytes needed for weights. It improves runtime only when the execution regime and kernel support let those saved bytes matter.
The elapsed time from arrival to response includes waiting, host work, and model execution. The target applies to the complete request.
Requests wait when arrivals compete for busy resources. Near saturation, small increases in utilization can produce large increases in waiting.
Grouping requests shares fixed work and can reuse weights. It can improve capacity while adding formation delay; the useful batch is constrained by latency and memory.
Service capacity is the rate at which the system can complete work under a specified workload. The latency target constrains how much of that capacity can be used.
Resident weights compete with KV state for device memory. Reducing weight storage can free cache capacity, subject to runtime allocations.
Attention keys and values retained for one conversation grow with its token count and model geometry.
Longer histories retain more token state. At fixed cache format and model geometry, the per-conversation KV footprint grows linearly.
Each generation step reads retained attention state and appends state for a new token.
Execution includes arithmetic and moving operands. A resource bound gives a lower limit; profiling explains additional overhead.
Utilization compares offered work with available service capacity. High utilization leaves little room for variation in arrivals and execution.
A request may wait while the server collects a batch. This delay spends latency allowance before the model runs.
The device memory left after weights and other resident state bounds the cache pool.
Memory remaining after model weights must hold the attention state of every resident conversation.
The number of training examples contributing to a parameter update; it affects execution efficiency and the updates required to reach target quality.
